newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Some verdicts in Bahrain coup trial soon.
newsitem.headline: Some verdicts in Bahrain coup trial soon.

text.p: Bahrain's state security court has said it will listen in a few days to final defence statements in the trial of 81 people accused of involvement in an alleged pro-Iranian plot to topple the government by force.
Lawyers said they expected some verdicts to be given later in the week and some suspects could face the death penalty.
Local newspapers on Sunday quoted a statement by the court as saying final defence statements would be given on Wednesday.
The trial started in the Gulf Arab state on March 1. Lawyers said 59 of the suspects were appearing before the court and the rest were being tried in absentia.

The defendants are accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Political parties are banned in Bahrain.
Bahrain in June accused Iran of backing an attempt to topple the government by force. Iran denied the charge and said it was not interfering in the internal affairs of Bahrain.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged a campaign of bombings, arson attacks, sabotage and riots since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms by the Sunni Moslem rulers. At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested since then.
